change_rows.note: THE STRONGEST CHANGE ROW AVAILABLE: a NEW event kind. The control build has no fallpath.mjs, so _fall_path is unemittable on control. This cannot be a row control emits too -- the defect that falsely reverted three canaries (change-row-must-discriminate).

exposure.note: ARITHMETIC. 5 bots x 180 min = 15 bot-h. The instrument's own measured yield on 17-18 Sep was 1.338 rows/bot-h -> 20.1 rows expected, so a floor of 8 is 40% of the point estimate and comfortably reachable. A row-stream reconstruction on the CURRENT build (2026-09-25, 480 bot-h, 80 bots) puts a LOWER BOUND of 0.069 triggers/bot-h -> 1.0 rows, because the real trigger fires on the bot's `health` event stream and `onGround`, neither of which is logged; the reconstruction can only see health at telemetry-row times (median gap 2.0 s vs the 1 s peak sampler). The floor is therefore set against the instrument's own measurement, not the proxy, and the 19x spread between them is why final_on_zero_exposure is INCONCLUSIVE and not a verdict.

own_lines.note: The change row must not appear on control. A non-zero here means pool contamination or a failed teardown of an earlier canary, not an effect.

primary.note: THERE IS NO PRODUCTIVITY PRIMARY, BECAUSE THE CHANGE CANNOT MOVE PRODUCTIVITY. The only question a fall-path recorder can answer about itself is whether its rows are READABLE: the share of _fall_path rows whose descent association resolves to ACTIVE or none rather than `unknown`. REPORT-ONLY: no backtest exists for this line, and CLAUDE.md forbids a rule reverting anything before gatecal/guardcal give it a false-revert rate.

Re-measured 2026-09-25: 1,611 B per long-detail row (measured mean of _death rows, n=8; the fall row's detail is budgeted at 290 chars by ROW_BUDGET and the logger truncates at 300), 903.3 MB/day raw uncompressed at 80 bots (measured, yesterday's rotated generation, 80 files). The original claim of 0.58% was against an implied 714 MB/day; raw has grown 26%, so the share is now LOWER and the claim is conservative.

mechanism_check.note: Same field as the exposure floor, on purpose: this change has exactly one mechanism -- a row reaching the log. If the rows are absent the change did nothing, and no other line can rescue it. Guards against the canary-can-ship-inert failure (owner-01 ran 97 min as the baseline).

safety.floor: TWO canary deaths AND > 1.25x the control rate
safety.note: THE ONLY DECIDING SAFETY RULE, and the one that got this wrong last time. falls-01 was reverted on 2 deaths -- which met the letter of the two-death floor -- while neither death was a fall and one bot had drowned identically in the PRE window on the baseline. gatecal measured the two-death rule falsely reverting 46% of harmless canaries. A death on an OBSERVABILITY-ONLY change is a coincidence by construction: name it, do not let it revert. Every death must be read for mechanism before it counts.

pool_draw: AT DEPLOY TIME, not from history: 5 bots drawn at random from the stratum of bots with non-zero descent activity in the preceding 180 min, control = the rest. The pool must CONTAIN the population the fix targets (a fall recorder in a pool that never falls shows nothing), but NOT the argmax -- picking the highest-baseline pool builds in reversion.
teardown: THREE steps: drop-ins, clearing canary_pool, AND restarting the pool's bots staggered 12 s apart, then confirm exactly two versions live. Also restore the golden analysis lib from ~/mcai-analysis/lib/ afterwards -- a deploy by any path other than ~/bin/fleet-deploy does not restore it, which is how the efa2853 promotion reverted telemetry.py, openloop.py and version_split.py at 11:57Z today.

The log-volume RATE input is unresolved, not measured: the trigger depends on the health event stream and onGround, neither of which is logged, so it cannot be re-measured without deploying the instrument. Only the denominators were re-measured.
